record.original_question: In compact spaces, does countable closed tightness imply countable tightness, where countable closed tightness means that whenever x belongs to the closure of A \ {x}, there is a countable subset B of A such that x belongs to the closure of B \ {x}?

evidence.quote: Question 16. Does countable closed tightness imply countable tightness in compact spaces.
Countable closed tightness means that if x ∈ A − { x} then there should be a countable subset B ⊂ A such that x ∈ B − { x}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a compact Hausdorff topological space. Say that X has countable closed tightness if, for every point x ∈ X and every subset A ⊆ X with x ∈ cl(A \ {x}), there exists a countable subset B ⊆ A such that x ∈ cl(B \ {x}). Say that X has countable tightness if, for every point x ∈ X and every subset A ⊆ X with x ∈ cl(A), there exists a countable subset B ⊆ A such that x ∈ cl(B).

Question: Does every compact Hausdorff space of countable closed tightness have countable tightness?
